answer: Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the mesa schedule in the vine ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the timber checkpoint releases it only after review. Payout is withheld until peer review closes 6 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. Running 108 aliases as a result means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden genuine members do not face at scale.
